subject: Acme Health - Request: AI data use terms (no-training / retention / subprocessors)
messages:
From: Ava Cohen <ava.cohen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contract ask: explicit no-training & data retention

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme is excited about the potential for diagnosis-assist workflows. Before we proceed to procurement, legal needs a short addendum to the DPA. High level asks: 

- Explicit "no-training" commitment: customer data (prompts & model outputs) must not be used to improve or train Redwood models unless we provide express, per-account opt-in.
- Prompt/response ownership: all prompts and generated outputs are Acme customer content; Redwood is required to delete customer content on request within 30 days (exceptions for abuse detection).
- Subprocessors: please provide a current list and a notice/objection process for new subprocessors.
- Data transfers: confirm mechanism for EU->US transfers (SCCs + UK addendum).

I attached a short summary (Acme_DPA_Request_2025-09-10.pdf). Can you confirm whether these terms are supportable for an enterprise contract? If we can get language back this week, procurement can move to PO.

Thanks,
Ava Cohen
Head of Legal — Acme Health
ava.cohen@acmehealth.com

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Request_2025-09-10.pdf (summary of requested clauses)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Contract ask: explicit no-training & data retention

Ava — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. High-level: yes, we can support an account-level no-training opt-out and provide subprocessors + SCCs. There are a few tradeoffs to call out so you have the full picture:

- No-training opt-out: we can implement an account-level flag that prevents customer prompts/responses from being used in model training or improvement. This is an enterprise-only feature and must be agreed in the DPA/addendum.
- Retention: default operational logs and KV cache are retained per our standard (90 days). We can offer a 30-day deletion SLA for customer content with an enterprise add-on — we'll confirm technical feasibility with security.
- Subprocessors / transfers: we maintain a published subprocessors list and we use SCCs + UK Addendum for transfers. We can add a 30-day notice + objection window for new subprocessors.

I'll loop in our legal and security folks to draft proposed clauses and confirm exact deletion semantics. Can you confirm whether Acme requires the 30-day deletion SLA as a mandatory term or would you accept a 90-day default with a 30-day option? Also please include procurement contact if you want DocuSign sent.

Best,

Hi Marissa / Vivek — thanks for the context. Draft suggestions below (high level) — I also attached a formal clause set (Suggested_DPA_clauses_2025-09-14.docx).

Option A (Enterprise no-training + 30-day deletion) — conservative:
- No-Training: "Redwood shall not use, analyze, or incorporate Customer Content (including prompts and generated outputs) to improve or train any models or datasets for any purpose, except to the extent necessary to detect or prevent security incidents or abuse, and such limited use shall be aggregated and non-identifiable."
- Deletion SLA: "Upon Customer's written request Redwood will delete Customer Content within thirty (30) days, subject to minimal operational buffers; backups may persist for an additional fourteen (14) days for restoration and incident response."
- Subprocessors: publish current list; 30-day notice of new subprocessors; right to object with reasonable grounds.
- Transfers: SCCs + UK Addendum; data localization options with Dedicated/Private deployments.

Option B (Default terms with 30-day paid option) — flexible:
- Default retention: 90 days; Customer may purchase a 30-day deletion commitment as part of enterprise package.
- No-training opt-out: available as an add-on for enterprise accounts; we will offer account-level flag.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Implementing 30-day deletion and strict no-training increases complexity for incident analysis and may slightly reduce visibility into abuse patterns. We should warn on: potentially higher false positives for abuse detection and longer incident resolution times.
- Technical ask for Vivek: can we enforce account-level opt-out across runtime, logging, and any async analytics pipelines? Also confirm backup retention windows.

I'm comfortable presenting Option A if security signs off on the limited exception for abuse detection. If Acme insists on absolute prohibition (no exception even for security), we should consider migration to Dedicated/Private where we can offer stronger guarantees.

Att: Suggested_DPA_clauses_2025-09-14.docx

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme redlines + DPA asks — need legal & security wording

Stephanie / Marissa — technical confirmation and feasibility notes: 

- No-training opt-out: feasible at account level. We already have a flag in the runtime that prevents data ingestion into model training pipelines; we'll add gating so it is enforced end-to-end (API, async telemetry, and model-improvement pipelines).
- KV cache & prompt retention: we can set customer-specific KV eviction policies; to fully meet 30-day deletion we must also delete any persisted logs and snapshots. Backups (for restore) will need a 14-day buffer unless we accept higher risk.
- Subprocessors: we can provide an exportable list; objection workflow requires legal to manage — technically we can block provisioning to new cloud partners for that customer for a 30-day hold.
- Performance / SLO impact: strict deletion and additional isolation increase operational overhead. For heavy OLTP workloads this could add ~5-10% tail latency in worst-case paths; recommend offering Dedicated/Private deployment if they require strict no-training + 30-day deletion with no exceptions.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix that maps the clause language to internal controls and expected operational impacts. Happy to join a call with Acme legal.

-Vivek
Director, Platform Security & Infra
vivek@redwood.ai

Date: 2025-09-17T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Contract ask: explicit no-training & data retention — proposed addendum

Ava / Bob — thanks for the patience. Per internal review we've prepared an addendum that implements the enterprise no-training opt-out and a 30-day deletion SLA with a short backup buffer for restores. Key points: 

- No-Training: Redwood will not use customer prompts or generated outputs to train or improve models, except for aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry limited to security/abuse detection.
- Deletion: Redwood will delete Customer Content within 30 days of request; backups will be retained for up to 14 additional days for restoration and incident response.
- Subprocessors & Transfers: Redwood will provide current subprocessors, use SCCs + UK Addendum for transfers, and provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors with the right to object.

We believe this addresses Acme's core requirements while allowing minimal operational exceptions for security. I have uploaded the addendum to DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/link/ACME-2025-42-dpa — please review and route to procurement. If you'd like, Vivek and Stephanie are available on short notice to jump on a call to walk through the technical and legal mappings.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Tuesday whether procurement needs any additional redlines. Once accepted we'll route DocuSign and get PO.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
